stories.title: SSGC announces winter gas supply schedule for Sindh, Balochistan
summary: KARACHI: The Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) on Wednesday announced the gas supply schedule for the winter season, under which three slots have been fixed for supply to domestic consumers, in line with federal government directives.

Gas availability under new schedule: 6:30am-9am (Breakfast) 12pm-2:30pm (Lunch) 6pm-9pm (Dinner) The SSGC shared the schedule on its website and social media platforms, saying that it was “prioritising domestic consumers by ensuring supply during meal times”.
For the past some years, SSGC’s consumers have not been getting round-the-clock gas supply.

stories.title: US midterms: Democrats win US Congress in midterm rout of Trump
summary: Democrat James Talarico ousted a Trump-backed Senate candidate, while Gina Hinojosa unseated Republican governor Greg Abbott, ending decades of Republican control of the state’s top office.
In California, Democrat Xavier Becerra handily defeated Donald Trump-backed Republican Steve Hilton in the race to become the governor, US networks said.

Democrats held onto three House districts in Florida that Republican lawmakers had redrawn earlier this year, all of which backed Trump by at least nine percentage points, according to media projections.

stories.title: Israel election commission rejects Netanyahu charges of fraud
summary: Israeli electoral authorities on Wednesday rejected allegations promoted by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of fraud by Arab parties, who could hold the key to removing him from power after a divisive vote.

He had earlier warned Netanyahu against launching a new war with his close ally US President Donald Trump against Iran, which could help the Israeli prime minister push for a unity government or to run out the clock until new elections.

stories.title: Numbers that tell the story of the Democrats' midterm blowout
summary: Young voters, Latinos turn away Young men and Latino voters — two segments of the American electorate crucial to Trump — turned sharply away from the president and his Republican Party, exit polls showed.
